purpose: GATE 1.5 supplement only: add two-layer deepening for B-line after REVIEWER Round 3, without claiming new physics or validation.

status_guardrail.current_claim_level: measurement protocol plus reproducible synthetic benchmark
status_guardrail.forbidden_claim: Do not claim that amorphous band-like transport has a newly discovered graph mechanism.
status_guardrail.allowed_claim: The B-line is a predeclared residual-prediction protocol comparing mobility-edge/Ioffe-Regel controls against In-s graph/connectivity/O-O defect metrics on the same samples with external labels.

lp29_protocol_connection.null_model_A: External observables are explained by mobility-edge/Ioffe-Regel style diagnostics and standard controls: carrier density, EF_minus_Ec, kF_l or independent l/TCR/activation labels, onsite variance, mstar, tau, oxygen-vacancy proxy, finite-size and batch controls.
lp29_protocol_connection.candidate_model_B: Structure-derived In-s graph metrics M(X)={S_GC,z_eff,lambda_2,rho_A,edge/corner motif ratios,O-O defect fraction,high-betweenness damage} are tested only for residual predictive power beyond the null controls.
lp29_protocol_connection.external_labels: Y must be Hall, Drude/optical, Wannier/QSGW, spectral linewidth/IPR, or matched-control residual labels not generated by the same graph proxy used to define M(X).
lp29_protocol_connection.reviewer_constraint: Synthetic recovery of graph rules is diagnostic-only and cannot validate B.

deepening_1_layer_1.core_idea: Treat the mobility-edge/Ioffe-Regel diagnosis and the In-s connectivity diagnosis as two projections of the same sample-level operator only at the protocol level, not as an established material fact.

math_structure.graph: G(X)=(V,E,w) from same-sample structure X, with w_ij=t0*exp(-(r_ij-r0)/lambda)*(1+alpha_edge*I_edge+alpha_corner*I_corner)*exp(-beta*f_OO,ij).
operators: A_w: weighted adjacency on In sites
H_graph=diag(epsilon_i)+A_w: diagnostic graph Hamiltonian, not an external validation label
P_controls: projection onto mobility-edge/Ioffe-Regel and nuisance-control feature space

deepening_1_layer_1.protocol_test: Fit external labels Y with controls first, then test whether graph-spectral features predict residuals: r_Y=Y-hatY_controls. B is only supported if r_Y has stable out-of-sample dependence on graph-spectral features.
deepening_1_layer_1.non_claim: This layer does not prove mobility edge is caused by the graph. It only defines a sharper residual test for whether mobility-edge controls are losing information that graph spectra retain.

deepening_1_layer_2.direction: residualization after mobility-edge controls plus targeted attack
deepening_1_layer_2.deeper_math_structure: Use orthogonalized residual operators and adversarial graph perturbations. Let M_perp=(I-P_controls)M(X), where P_controls spans n, EF_minus_Ec, Ioffe-Regel variables, onsite variance, mstar, tau, oxygen-vacancy proxy, finite-size, and batch terms. The B question becomes whether M_perp has predictive content for Y_perp=(I-P_controls)Y.

targeted_attack_formalization.random_attack: Delete or weaken O-O/coordination-associated edges uniformly at fixed total f_OO or fixed deleted-edge count.
targeted_attack_formalization.targeted_attack: Delete or weaken edges ranked by vulnerability V_e=b_e*|w_e|/t0, where b_e is edge betweenness centrality.
targeted_attack_formalization.diagnostic_contrast: Delta_attack = loss(Y_proxy or external residual under targeted attack) - loss(under random attack at matched damage budget).
targeted_attack_formalization.external_label_requirement: If attack is performed only inside H_graph, Delta_attack remains a diagnostic. It becomes evidence only when the same edge-vulnerability statistic predicts external Hall/Drude/Wannier/spectral residuals.

predeclared_signs: partial residual mobility or Drude weight should increase with z_eff, S_GC, lambda_2, and rho_A after controls.
partial residual mobility or Drude weight should decrease with high-betweenness O-O damage V_target after controls.
Targeted high-V_e damage should be worse than random damage at matched f_OO if the B-line is more than renamed disorder.
deepening_1_layer_2.non_claim: The targeted-attack structure is a falsification device. It is not a claim that real O-O defects have already been shown to perform targeted attacks in amorphous In2O3.

deepening_2_layer_1.direction: measurement protocol generalization: same-sample external labels
deepening_2_layer_1.core_idea: Promote the B-line from a graph intuition to a locked same-sample data protocol. Every row must join one sample or one atomistic snapshot to both baseline diagnostics and external observables.

model_comparison.baseline: Y_external ~ n + EF_minus_Ec + Ioffe_Regel_metric + onsite_variance + mstar + tau_proxy + oxygen_vacancy_proxy + finite_size + batch
model_comparison.graph_added: Y_external ~ baseline_terms + S_GC + z_eff + lambda_2 + rho_A + edge_corner_ratio + f_OO + high_betweenness_damage
model_comparison.locked_success_condition: Graph-added model must improve held-out prediction or residual sign stability on external labels; otherwise B remains a nonvalidated descriptor.

deepening_2_layer_1.non_claim: A same-sample table is required before using words such as validated, mechanism, or discovery.

deepening_2_layer_2.direction: negative controls, leave-one-composition-out, and perturbation attack

negative_controls: Degree-preserving rewired graph metrics at fixed degree sequence and weight histogram.
Randomized O-O defect positions at fixed total f_OO.
Onsite-only disorder controls at matched onsite variance.
Srivastava-style orbital-overlap baseline to test whether LP29 graph metrics are only a reparameterization.
Hall-derived predictors flagged and excluded when predicting the same Hall target.
deeper_protocol_generalization.leave_one_composition_or_family_out: Train on all but one composition/family, e.g. a-In2O3, ITO, IGZO, or AIMD structure family; test on the held-out family. Passing only within one family is weaker and should be reported as non-generalized.
perturbation_attack: Random edge weakening at matched deleted-edge count.
High-betweenness edge weakening ranked by V_e.
Motif-specific weakening of edge-sharing or corner-sharing layers.
O-O defect guided weakening using only structural positions, not the target observable.
deeper_protocol_generalization.pass_fail_logic: B survives this layer only if real or independently computed labels show the targeted/motif-aware graph terms predict residual changes that negative controls do not.

deepening_2_layer_2.non_claim: Failure under leave-one-composition-out does not falsify all graph descriptors, but it forbids broad claims about amorphous oxides. Success in synthetic perturbations alone is still not validation.

unit_notes: t0 and w_ij have energy units, e.g. eV.
r_ij, r0, and lambda are lengths; exponential arguments are dimensionless.
alpha_edge, alpha_corner, beta, f_OO, b_e, S_GC, z_eff/t0-normalized degree, lambda_2 after chosen normalization, and V_e are dimensionless unless explicitly reported otherwise.

items: External mobility, Drude weight, and ridge coherence are predicted to increase with z_eff, S_GC, lambda_2, and rho_A after controls.
External residual mobility/Drude/ridge coherence are predicted to decrease with high-betweenness O-O damage.
Increasing t_min deletes weak edges in a fixed graph, so kept-edge S_GC and kept-edge z_eff should not increase under that threshold operation.
Current B Round 3 data status is synthetic toy benchmark only.
Required validation data are same-sample external Hall/Drude/Wannier/spectral labels or matched-control residuals.
Jankousky raw structures/QSGW subset, Furubayashi digitized transport table, or Aliano-style AIMD fallback remain data-acquisition targets, not completed validation in this supplement.
Same-sample IDs can be joined across structural descriptors and external labels.
Mobility-edge/Ioffe-Regel controls are computed before graph residual tests and are not tuned post hoc to lose.
Graph metrics are computed from structure only and do not use target labels.
Hall-factor and linewidth conventions are locked before regression.
Negative controls and leave-one-family tests are predeclared.

limitations: Without real same-sample external-label data, graph metrics are not validated.
The existing B-line synthetic benchmark is useful for reproducibility and sanity checks only; it cannot establish material physics.
LP29 cannot currently claim a new mechanism for amorphous band-like transport.

Prior art already covers mobility edges, Ioffe-Regel tests, amorphous oxide band transport, In-s orbital overlap, percolation/disorder transport, and Jankousky-style effective bands; LP29's remaining space is strict residual-comparison protocol.

If graph metrics fail against mobility-edge/Ioffe-Regel controls, Srivastava orbital-overlap controls, negative controls, or leave-one-composition-out tests, the B-line must be reported as nonvalidated or family-limited.
